title: HASANI v. "THE FORMER YUGOSLAV REPUBLIC OF MACEDONIA"
summary:
In Hasani v. "the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia," the applicant, Ms Emrana Hasani, is a stateless person born in Kosovo in 1986 who settled in Macedonia as a minor after fleeing Kosovo in 1999. While the judgment does not explicitly confirm her Roma identity, Ms Hasani referred to reports highlighting the difficulties Roma face in obtaining personal identification documents in Kosovo, suggesting her connection to the Roma and Traveller communities. The case centered on her vulnerability as a stateless person at risk of expulsion to Kosovo, where she claimed she would face discrimination and practical obstacles, particularly due to her lack of identification documents and her fear of persecution.

After years of asylum in Macedonia, Ms Hasani’s status was revoked in 2007, and she was ordered to leave the country. Despite having four children with a Macedonian national, she was repeatedly instructed to regularize her status through marriage or by obtaining documents from Kosovo, which she argued was impossible due to her statelessness and fear of return. Domestic courts upheld the termination of her asylum, finding no evidence of a real risk of inhuman or degrading treatment if she returned to Kosovo.

The European Court of Human Rights examined her complaints under Articles 3, 8, and 13 of the Convention but declared the application inadmissible. The Court found that Ms Hasani had not substantiated a real risk of treatment contrary to Article 3 and had not exhausted available remedies to regularize her status. No violation was found, and no remedies were awarded.
